Start classification table of spec 0003 (what the journal reader found, crossed with whether the configuration carries the authority witness)
AuthorityState Held: the witness equals the authority ID and the hold is restore_pending; Closed with authority.restore_pending
AuthorityState Mismatch: the journal is Present but the witness differs from its authority ID; Closed with authority.mismatch
AuthorityState Missing: the witness is set but the journal is Absent; Closed with authority.missing

AuthorityState Ready: the witness equals the authority ID and the hold is none; the only state that carries an Authority; the ten writer admission checks run only when the witness of the configuration passed to writer_admission still matches the authority ID of the state
AuthorityState Unconfirmed: the journal is Present but the configuration carries no witness; Closed with authority.unconfirmed
AuthorityState Uninitialized: the journal is Absent and there is no witness; admission is Closed with authority.uninitialized
AuthorityState Unreadable: the file cannot be opened, is not a POOL journal, has a newer schema, fails its integrity check or holds an inconsistent StoredAuthority; Closed with authority.unreadable
Journal table store: one singleton row with authority_id (16 byte BLOB), authority_revision, start_sequence, hold (none or restore_pending) and created_unix_ms
Authority struct: private; only classify_startup makes one, so no state other than Ready can lead to an open admission
AuthorityState enum (Uninitialized, Unconfirmed, Missing, Unreadable, Mismatch, Held, Ready(Authority)); only Ready carries an Authority
AuthorityId type (pool-config: 16 bytes, in text exactly 32 characters from 0 to 9 and a to f; names one journal and is not a secret)

BootstrapPlan struct: private; one ApprovedTopology per cluster with the expected_writer, the configured system identifier, the timeline the writer reported, epoch 1, every configured node as a member and no conflict latch
Hold enum (None, RestorePending): the restore hold a journal carries when it came out of a supported backup
StoreProbe enum (Absent, Unreadable, Present(StoredAuthority)): what the journal reader found; in the product only the journal reader that scope 004 places in pool-control builds one
StoredAuthority struct (authority_id, authority_revision, start_sequence, hold, clusters, quarantine) with public fields, because the journal reader has to fill it

Walk 1 clean startup (test walk_clean_startup): the first start is Uninitialized and closed; bootstrap plans main with writer pg1, timeline 1, epoch 1 or is refused (rows 2a to 2e); after bootstrap the state is Unconfirmed until the operator adds the witness, then Ready and Open

Walk 2 missing journal (test walk_missing_journal): a journal that is gone is Missing, a damaged one is Unreadable, another daemon's is Mismatch, and bootstrap is refused; the two ways out are restoring a backup or a deliberate new bootstrap, which forgets the quarantine and every membership decision

Bootstrap in spec 0003: the only way a journal comes into being; an explicit operator command, the daemon never creates a journal, so an empty directory authorizes nothing; stricter than admission because it needs every node once; the scope 004 command writes the journal in one transaction with a new random authority ID, revision 1, start sequence 0 and hold none, and prints the ID

Fresh rule of spec 0003: per node the observation with the latest sampled_at counts (a tie is no evidence); it is fresh when sampled_at is not later than now and its age is less than the expiry; a stale or Failed observation is no evidence

Spec 0003 writer admission rule added with AC-16: a Ready state belongs to the configuration it was classified with; in Ready writer_admission first compares the witness of the configuration it was given with the authority ID of the state: none gives authority.unconfirmed, another gives authority.mismatch, reported alone, observations not read, latches_conflict() false; the journal identity is compared at every admission

Tradeoff of spec 0003: after a bootstrap, and again after a reconcile, the operator must copy the authority ID into the configuration before POOL admits anything; that step tells a first start from a lost journal
Tradeoff of spec 0003: a new bootstrap after a lost journal forgets the quarantine and every membership decision

Validation time rule of spec 0003: the work of pool-config code in validate grows no faster than file size times its logarithm, for every file within the limit, valid or not, including turning a span into line and column; never count from the top of the file or the start of a line once per entry, value or finding; a table of line starts alone is not enough for a file with every entry on one line

Why 10 seconds (0003 AC-15; Apple M1 Max, debug build, 2026-11-15): correct code takes 0.34 to 0.39 s per input; the Build plan step 3 code that counted from the top for every value took 241 s for 16000 nodes, about 165 s for input 1; the limit lies about 25 times above the first and 16 times below the second; a miss is reported as a finding with the measured time, the number is not raised

The 10 second limit of 0003 AC-15: each validate call on made input 1, 2 or 3 and each run of the built binary on input 3 returns within 10 seconds, measured by the test with std::time::Instant in the debug build (validate never reads a clock); no ratio of two timings; the test cannot stop a slow call (rule W3 allows no thread), so it checks the time after each input

Writer admission reason 1, authority.cluster_unknown: the journal has no approved topology for this cluster, or the configuration has no such cluster; reported alone

Writer admission reason 2, authority.config_conflict: expected_writer is not the approved writer, or the configured system identifier is not the one in the journal, or a journal member is not a configured node of this cluster
Writer admission reason 3, authority.conflict_latched: the conflict latch of the cluster is set in the journal
Writer admission reason 4, authority.writer_quarantined: the approved writer is in the quarantine of its cluster
Writer admission reason 9, evidence.second_primary: another configured node, not quarantined, with a fresh observation and the system identifier of the journal reports that it is not in recovery
Writer admission reason 10, evidence.timeline_ahead: another configured node, not quarantined, with a fresh observation reports a timeline greater than the one the journal recorded for the writer
Writer admission reason 6, evidence.writer_identity: the approved writer reports another system identifier than the journal
Writer admission reason 7, evidence.writer_in_recovery: the approved writer reports that it is in recovery
Writer admission reason 5, evidence.writer_missing: there is no fresh Reached observation of the approved writer; checks 6 to 8 are then skipped
Writer admission reason 8, evidence.writer_timeline: the approved writer reports another timeline than the journal recorded
Record Membership decision (maintenance, drain, detach): pool-control, set and cleared by operations; SQLite; loaded before any lease is admitted; built in 008 and 009

Record Quarantine: pool-control, set by a promotion or an operator and cleared only by an operation with rejoin evidence; a healthy probe cannot clear it (PRD-006 AC-3); SQLite; model in 003, first writer in 010

The small domain of 0003 AC-12 (test open_only_on_full_agreement in admission_model.rs): 8192 combinations of expected_writer, approved writer, pg3 quarantine, conflict latch and eight observations per node, compared with an expected answer computed by a rule written separately from the code under test

Closed struct: private and never empty; reasons() gives each ClosedReason at most once, latches_conflict() says whether the daemon must set the conflict latch

Walk 3 conflicting role evidence (test walk_conflicting_evidence): rows a to p from a Ready state; only full agreement opens; rows c, d and i latch a conflict; an unrecorded promotion never adopts pg2; rows j and k stay Open; row k, a quarantined node that reports itself as a primary, is the one exception to the letter of PRD-006 AC-2

Walk 4 restore of a backup taken before a promotion (test walk_restore_before_promotion): a supported backup carries the hold restore_pending and is Held; raw copies are caught by config conflict, missing writer, second primary or timeline ahead; the way out is the reconcile operation of scope 009, which gives the journal a new authority ID

Conflict latch rule (spec 0003): Closed::latches_conflict() is true for evidence.second_primary or evidence.timeline_ahead; the daemon of scope 004 then sets the latch in the journal in one transaction; admission stays closed with authority.conflict_latched until an operation clears it (PRD-006 AC-2); an observation can add this restriction and never remove one
A member cannot be dropped by editing the file (spec 0003): a configuration that no longer lists a journal member is a conflict; removing a member is the detach operation of scope 009

What a mutation compares (spec 0003): every durable mutation is one SQLite transaction that starts with BEGIN IMMEDIATE, reads the compared value again and writes nothing when it differs (PRD-006 AC-1); the table lists bootstrap, daemon start, conflict latch, reload, membership changes, reconcile and change of approved writer with the precondition each names

Positive conflict closes, silence about a replica does not (spec 0003): a second primary or a node on a later timeline closes writes; a replica that is down, slow or not yet probed does not, or one dead replica would stop every write

Quarantine is the reviewed answer (spec 0003): a quarantined node that reports itself as a primary, or a later timeline, does not close writes to the approved writer (checks 9 and 10 leave it out) and never becomes eligible by itself; an exception to the letter of PRD-006 AC-2 for a quarantined node only (decision 17; wording added on 2026-11-15 after review finding d1, the rule did not change)
Tradeoff of spec 0003: until scope 009 exists nothing clears a conflict latch and nothing removes a member, so such a cluster stays closed until the member is put back or the operator bootstraps anew
[[cluster]] table keys: cluster[].id (ClusterId, unique), cluster[].system_identifier (a string in SystemIdentifier syntax), cluster[].expected_writer (a NodeId naming a node of this cluster)
Key cluster[].expected_writer: the operator's statement of which node is the writer; it seeds the approved writer at bootstrap and must keep agreeing with the journal, or writes stay closed
Record Cluster: pool-config ClusterConfig, read by both planes; from the configuration file; read and validated again at restart, nothing remembered; built in 003
ClusterId type (pool-config identifier: 1 to 63 bytes, the first a to z, the rest a to z, 0 to 9, _ or -; built by parse)
EligiblePrimary struct: the private result of an Open admission, with cluster(), node(), topology_epoch() and authority_revision()
SystemIdentifier type (pool-config: the PostgreSQL system identifier, a whole number from 1 to 18446744073709551615, decimal text with no leading zero)

What goes into a backend identity (the 0001 SC-2 pool key parts and their sources: cluster, endpoint node ID, database, actual login role, credential generation, topology epoch, TLS policy, startup profile); the configuration generation is checked at handoff and is not part of the key (PRD-002 AC-4)

Record Session: pool-core data plane, fields as in the data structures of PRD-001; made at accept, ends at disconnect or error; gone at restart, clients reconnect (0001 SC-5); built in 004

Tradeoff of spec 0003: AC-15 is a limit on wall clock time; a machine that stands still for seconds in the middle of a test can miss it, the tests take a second or two longer, and when the counting goes wrong again the test runs for minutes before it fails, where the CI job limit of 15 minutes may end it first; either way the check is red
Tradeoff of spec 0003: bootstrap needs every configured node reachable once; a node that is down has to be repaired or taken out of the configuration first
Tradeoff of spec 0003: the configuration is trusted; pointing the host of a node at another machine makes POOL probe that machine; the journal records node IDs, not addresses
Tradeoff of spec 0003: findings inside entries name the key and the place but still not the text
Tradeoff of spec 0003: pool-control is built before anything calls it, so its interface may need to change when scope 004 connects real inputs; the rules should not

Tradeoff of spec 0003: a raw file copy of the journal carries no hold; with the old writer up and unfenced and no node on the newer timeline reachable, POOL cannot tell and opens writes to the old writer; fencing and the supported backup are the protection; a rollback of the whole proxy VM is the same case
Tradeoff of spec 0003: a stale configuration without the witness together with a lost journal looks like a first start; bootstrap then still needs fitting evidence from every node

Journal table member: rows of (cluster_id, node_id) with changed_revision; it holds the nodes of each cluster, the approved writer among them
Journal table quarantine: rows of (cluster_id, node_id) with since_epoch, changed_revision and changed_unix_ms

AuthorityRevision type: the authority revision, one per journal, starts at 1 at bootstrap, advanced by every transaction that changes the approved topology, members, conflict latch, quarantine, a membership decision or the hold; survives restart; every durable mutation names the revision it expects

StartSequence type: the start sequence, one per journal, starts at 0 at bootstrap, advanced by each daemon start that finds its journal Ready before anything is admitted; survives restart; scopes every memory generation

TopologyEpoch type: the topology epoch, one per cluster, starts at 1 at bootstrap, advanced by a change of the approved writer (010) or a reconcile naming another writer (009); survives restart in the journal; compared by the pool key

Identifier and generation types (shared convention of spec 0003: one type per identifier and generation, built only by a checking function, a generation only reads, compares and advances by one and fails closed at the top, shared types live in pool-config, memory generations are scoped by the start sequence)
